The knowledgeable guide gave context to all of the history of the place, including its origins as a fort, as a trading post, and as the last stop for slaves before they were put on ships bound for the Americas. This is a must-see

Cape Coast Castle – A Journey Through History. Cape Coast Castle, located on Ghana’s central coast, is one of the most significant historical sites in West Africa. This UNESCO World Heritage Site stands as a powerful reminder of the transatlantic slave trade, offering visitors a deeply emotional and educational experience. Historical Significance Built by the Swedes in the 1650s and later controlled by the British, Cape Coast Castle was a major hub for the transatlantic slave trade. The castle’s dungeons, where enslaved Africans were held before being shipped to the Americas, leave a haunting impression. Walking through these dark, airless rooms gives a chilling glimpse into the suffering endured by countless men and women. Tour Experience Guided tours are available, led by knowledgeable guides who provide a detailed and moving account of the castle’s history. The Door of No Return, through which captives were forced onto slave ships, is one of the most powerful stops on the tour. However, there is also the Door of Return, symbolizing the resilience of African descendants who revisit their ancestral homeland. Architecture & Scenic Views Beyond its somber history, the castle itself is an impressive structure, featuring whitewashed walls and breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean. The contrast between the beauty of the surroundings and the tragic history within the walls adds to the site’s emotional impact. Museum & Exhibits The on-site museum provides valuable context with artifacts, documents, and displays about the slave trade, Ghanaian culture, and colonial history. It’s a great addition to the tour, helping visitors gain a deeper understanding of the past. Verdict Cape Coast Castle is a must-visit for history enthusiasts, students, and anyone seeking to understand the impact of the transatlantic slave trade. While the experience can be heavy and emotional, it is an important reminder of history and resilience. The only drawback is that the site can get crowded during peak tourist seasons, and some areas could use better maintenance. Final Thoughts A visit to Cape Coast Castle is not just a tour—it’s an unforgettable lesson in history, humanity, and remembrance. Highly recommended for anyone traveling to Ghana

Moving tour of infamous fortress, part of the transatlantic slave trade. A tour of Elmina Castle is a must for any visitor to Ghana who is interested in history and an understanding of the infamous slave trade. Dating from 1482, this is the oldest surviving fortress in sub Saharan Africa that housed captured slaves headed for the Americas. To take a guided tour of the “castle” and its slave dungeons, including the Door of No Return, is both fascinating and incredibly moving, affording insights into the horrific slave trade in ways that cannot be appreciated through books or even films

Haunting. Elmina Castle was one of the hundreds of holding prisons for black men, women and children who had been kidnapped and were about to be shipped to other parts of the world as slaves, never to return to their home and families. Our excellent guide gave much information about this trade and what it would have been like for these people. It horrified and haunted us. I had heard quite a bit about the slave trade, but not fully understood the size and horror of this mass kidnapping and displacement of people, over so long a period of time and by so many countries occupying Africa at the time. This important part of history warrants greater acknowledgement and understanding

Features personal items, photos, and a new digital walkthrough detailing his life and achievements.. The Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and Mausoleum is an impressive attraction and is one of the most modern structures we encountered in Ghana on our visit. The park was built in dedication to Ghana's first president, and you can learn about his life and legacy. It is one of the most popular tourist attractions in the country, and the park holds immense cultural and historical significance. The statues, gardens, fountains and mausoleum are modern, well-kept and well worth a visit. It was also great to see a lot of school groups there, learning about their heritage. However, this archaic practice of not allowing photos in museums and other certain attractions is irritating

A Thoughtful and Relaxing Visit. My partner and I visited **Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park** while we were in Accra, and we both really enjoyed it. The park is peaceful and beautifully kept, with open spaces, fountains, and shaded areas that make it perfect for a relaxed stroll together. Seeing the mausoleum where **Kwame Nkrumah** is laid to rest was moving. Standing there, we both felt the weight of his role in Ghana’s independence. The museum gave us a deeper look into his life, with photos and personal items that made the history feel alive and personal. It’s easy to get to from High Street, and exploring it as a couple made the experience even more special. We could walk at our own pace, take in the sights, and talk about the history and legacy together. Overall, it’s a quiet, reflective place that we both would recommend for couples who enjoy history, culture, and a peaceful atmosphere

A Home Far Away From Home!. Vincent and his wife Anna run a beautiful, small hotel close to the Wli Waterfall. This was without a doubt the nicest place my friend and I stayed during our time in Ghana. From the very first moment, it truly felt like home. Vincent welcomed us not as guests, but as family. We spent many evenings talking, laughing, and sharing stories with him. He is incredibly kind, smart, and warm-hearted. And the food, there is simply no place where we ate better than here. We can honestly say that Anna is the best chef in Ghana. We couldn’t stop eating and ended up having all our meals at the hotel. The menu is extensive and filled with delicious Ghanaian specialties. Vincent also knew everything about the activities in the area and helped us plan all five of our days. From the hotel, everything was easy to reach, and the view from the road is breathtaking, with beautiful mountains and nature all around. We played football with the children, danced with Vincent’s kids, and relaxed in the comfortable hammocks, enjoying the peaceful atmosphere. This place is full of warmth, joy, and genuine connection. I would love to come back here one day. Lots of love, Malou (from the Netherlands)

The guy running the place (not the owner) didn't speak much English. I was surprised by this but we made do. Thought I was done speaking French after Togo. The food at the restaurant was 'ok'. They want you to order in advance. I came out for breakfast one day to an omelette which was already cold. On another occasion I ordered dinner earlier in the day. I did not specify a time. Later I told the guy he cold start making my food now. He pointed to my food which was already on the table getting cold. So make sure you specify a time. I also ate a meal at the German owned place, which was good. You have to pay per hour for internet. I already had a Ghana sim so didn't need to do this. I'd recommend you get one yourself. It's a fairly short walk to the entrance to the waterfalls. One day I just went to the lower falls. The next I did the Ghana loop and visited the upper falls, then the lower again. I'd recommend starting as early as you can manage. Vincent, the owner was very friendly and welcoming. This is a solid budget choice

The rooms had everything we needed at a very reasonable price. The food was lovely and we were made to feel so welcome by all the staff. The setting is incredibly peaceful and ideally located to explore the Wli waterfalls. The person who made our stay extra special, was Vincent, the owner. He really went above and beyond. Following our stay we were heading for Togo. He found out all of the information we needed and said he’d drive us to the nearest border crossing where we could get a visa. A weekend of waterfalls and hiking. I would strongly recommend this inn, it’s perfect for a couple of nights whilst you hike Wli waterfalls and Mount Afadjato. Price is good for the hotel - I paid 109 cedis for two nights, food is cheap, around 20-30 for a good meal, breakfast was included in the room rate which was great. The owner is extremely friendly and doesn’t possess the normal Ghanaian personality trait of everything being late for absolutely everything. He sorted the transport for us and he told us it would help him to pre order the food which was perfect because then we could set a time and it would be on the table as we wanted. The rooms are great, pillows are fantastic and the fan is strong enough to keep it at a nice temperature throughout the night. Running water is a small luxury in Ghana but this inn has plenty of it and it’s great to take a shower after a 6 hour hike in sweltering heat. If one decides to do the Wli waterfalls hike, do the upper falls walk without a guide, it’s difficult to some extent but provides you with great views and satisfaction once you reach the summit! Don’t get a tour guide, really not necessary plus extra expense. We did the climb up Mount Afadjato the following day and then descended to Tagbo falls which was superb. Vincent - (the owner of the inn) organised transport for us again and was a great help once more. Overall a great weekend away and my cheapest weekend in Ghana but most certainly one of my favourites, you’d be silly not to go and stay at the Wli Waterfalls Inn and climb the two mountains if you’re visiting Ghana

We clearly communicated we wanted to camp on top of the Wli Falls, but that unfortunately did not happen. We only saw the falls for a very short amount of time after we had to sleep in the village quite far away from the falls. Additionally, the guide left us waiting for quite some time on both days. In the end, a lot of poor communication and what was planned was not delivered. Still a very pretty environment. Please, be very very clear with all communication. And normally not someone to advise against booking with someone, but it was quite disappointing to have booked with Wisdom and Francis. Another guide next time!

Natur pur. Wir waren früh an der Kasse. Der Eintritt hat 80 Cedi gekostet. Außerem wird zusätzlich noch nach einer Spende gefragt. Unser Guide war ein junger Mann, der den Job nur nebenbei macht, um seine Familie zu unterstützen. Dafür, dass er keine Lust darauf hat, war er ein super Guide. Er hat viel erklärt und alle unsere Fragen beantwortet. Wir haben am Ende 50 Cedi Trinkgeld gegeben. An den kleinen Wasserfall waren wir nach einer leichten Wanderung nach 40 Minuten. Die Wanderung zu den upper falls war anstrengend und dauerte ca. 3h bzw. vom kleinen Wasserfall 2h - mit Fotostopp an einem Viewpoint und Pause an einer Art Altar. An beiden Wasserfällen kann man baden, aber das Wasser ist recht kalt. Direkt neben dem Kassenbereich ist ein kleines Restaurant. Nach der anstrengenden Wanderung haben wir uns für kleines Geld Fufu mit Chicken und ein Getränk gegönnt - 50 Cedi. Schöne Umgebung und ein sehr guter Ausgleich zu den chaotischen Städten
Fascinating insight into Asante history.. very knowledgeable and informative guide, luckily coincided with when V&A London gave back on a 3 year loan some truly beautiful gold jewellery

Must see if visiting Ghana and will be in Kumasi. The most recent 2 reviews I read describe this museum very accurately except there was not a gift shop that I saw. Maybe it was closed the day we went. For such a small place, there was a lot of history. I wish I could have taken pictures of the board that showed the history of the Asante royals and what happened to each of them. The British museum had currently loaned some of the artifacts they themselves admit they had stolen, back to Ghana. But, apparently they plan to take those back to England in a few months so you better get over there and see them while you can! However, the US has permanently returned the artifacts they had acquired, to the Ghanians. So, those you should be able to see even if you don't come for a while, There is more cool stuff in each room and plenty of interesting history. The Ashante royal family is also one of few African tribal kingdoms the British royals acknowledge and invited to the Queen's funeral. So, I learned a lot about this tribe from this museum

Asante history in a nutshell. While in Kumasi, I visited the Manhyia Palace Museum. The tour started with a short video on the history of the Asantes (yes this is the correct spelling). I learned about the rise of the Asante kingdom, the Asantehene, the Queen Mother and the resilience of the Asante warriors. This really set the pace for the rest of the tour which was quite informative and educational. Our tour guide led us through room after room and explained the significance (and importance) of each artifact such as original furniture, thrones, wax figures, gold ornaments and even a working refrigerator from 1974! However, please note that pictures and recordings are not allowed. Overall I left with a feeling of cultural awareness and empowerment; but most importantly, a connection to and an appreciation of these majestic people which I descended from. Tip - Schedule your visit for the same day of the Akwasidae Festival which is an experience in itself!

Ashante Museum: The Jamaican Connection!. The Manhyia Palace Museum is located in Kamsi, Ghana. The grounds of the museum and Palace were beautiful. On the grounds were several peacocks, art on the walls, a Peace Bell and a very large Indian Rubber tree. As we entered the museum there was an area where you saw a video on the the history and culture of the Ashante Kingdom. What stuck with me the most was that the royal succession, in Ghana, is matrilineal. Which means that the family line is traced through the mother. The colors of the Ashante tribe are gold, black, and green. My aha moment came when I realized the the colors of Jamaica are the same, and Jamaicans can trace their lineage to Ghana from the transatlantic slave trade. The museum has a gift shop. The only problem was that you cannot take pictures in the museum only outside on the grounds. Good day!

Bardzo ciekawe muzeum .. Głównym obiektem kompleksu muzealnego jest Pałac Manhyia. Tu mieli swą siedzibę królowie Królestwa Aszanti . Zgromadzono tu oryginalne sprzęty z wyposażenia pałacu i dużo cennych dla kultury i tradycji Aszanti "skarbów". Niestety pod żadnym pozorem nie wolno wewnątrz robić zdjęć . Zresztą na zewnątrz pałacu też są one w zasadzie zabronione . W niewielkim parku obok zwraca uwagę potężny , ponad stuletni figowiec i swobodnie spacerujące pawie . Tam także ustawiony jest [ w roku 2019 ] pamiątkowy dzwon . Poświęcony jest zmarłemu rok wcześniej byłemu sekretarzowi generalnemu ONZ Kofi Annanowi który urodził się w Kumasi . W muzealnym sklepie jest spory wybór afrykańskiego rękodzieła , magnesów i innych pamiątek w rozsądnych cenach

History told by its own people. Was more of group to friends trip. I love their gifts shop and the pricing is moderate. You get to learn a lot about the Ashanti history and not through a white man’s lens but from the people themselves which gives it a different perspective if you have studied Ashanti history in school. I would say it is a must for all who visit Kumasi to pass through

Führung im Schnelldurchlauf. Nur wegen dem Palast würde ich nicht nach Kumasi. Der Eintritt kostet 100 Cedi. Die Führung dauert ca. 30 Min. Ein Einführungsvideo habe ich nicht gesehen. Man darf keine Fotos machen. Es war zwar interessant etwas über die Ashanti Geschichte zu lernen, aber mir war die Führung zu kurz - der Guide hat alles im Schnelldurchlauf erklärt. Auch draußen muss man genau aufpassen, wie weit man das Gelände betritt. Es gibt noch einen Souvenirshop mit günstigen Preisen (Kartenzahlung möglich)

wer sich für Kultur interessiert, ein unbedingtes MUSS.. Hoch interessant, einen Enblick in die Ashanti Kultur zu bekommen. Die Führung durch einen Museumsangestellten war gut gemacht, und informativ. Leider ein absolutes fotografier Verbot

Palace Tour. It's a brief but very informative tour of the palace which was built by the British after they had burnt his other one down and sent the king into exile. It's a sad story of the brutality used on the people in order to subdue them, but it's also a glimpse into the organisation and community-mindedness of this ancient kingdom. Well worth a visit
Amazing History. The Manhyia Palace boasts of the rich culture of the Ashanti kingdom. it is an amazing place to learn about the struggles of the people of Ghana and the Ashantis

The guide makes the visit worthwhile. Small museum hosting some interesting cultural treasures. It is painful to see that the objects on display are gathering dust and not protected well enough from visitors and weather. Authorities should invest in climate control to maintain the cultural treasures it holds. In this case, the museum guide makes all the difference in terms of the experience, sharing interesting information and facts about the various objects on display

One not to miss in Kumasi!. Absolutely excellent museum. Small but perfectly formed as they say! It houses many asante artifacts from the olden days which all together tell a very interesting story. The guide who showed us round was very knowledgeable and informative
Compact but good. Never judge a museum by it’s size. This one is small but packed full of good information on the Ashanti empire. Well worth a stop

A must visit location. Great place. A guided tour is included as part of the price and the guide Keane was great - thorough and very knowledgeable. This place is definitely worth a visit to learn more about Ashanti history and customs
A small gem in the Cultural Center. This small building is in the Cultural Center. It includes items of crafts and historical items. Our guide was very knowledgeable

A Must Visit. The museum is an excellent place for discovering Ashante royal traditions, history of the Ashante people and culture. It's a small museum, so it won't take long, but the staff there give you a wealth of information. If I had the time, I would have gone back for a second visit, perhaps next time I'm in Kumasi. Definitely worth visiting

Fantastic museum on Ashanti History. They have great items here which are worth seeing and the guides are helpful. This is the location of the fake golden stool as well as other items of value and note

Knowledge is Power. I was overwhelmed with delight as I learned a lot with a stop at Ghana’s National Cultural Center where I was awash with pride learning about the Ashanti Kings and Queen mothers, their rise, fall and rise again from a knowledgeable and enthusiastic guide. The brave Queen who took on the British at the age of sixty was my favorite. The place replica is small but gives you an idea of what the real palace is like. It is full of ancient artifacts that the British hadn't stolen and the Ashanti people are proud at preserving their history. If you love history told from a non-European narrative this is a must do

Compact museum but comprehensive explanation. A guided tour is included in the admission fee of 10 GHS for foreigners. My guide, Adwoa, is very good. Well worth a visit if you are visiting the National Cultural Centre
History is Good!. This is an excellent place to visit to gain knowledge of the traditions and history of the Ashanti Royalty. My guide was extremely knowledgeable and answered all of my questions

Aburi Botanical Gardens, established in 1890, is a historic, scenic, and affordable nature escape located 32km from Accr. The Aburi Botanical Gardens, established in 1890, is a historic,135-year-old, colonial-era garden in Ghana's Eastern Region offering a peaceful, cooler alternative to Accra. Visitors typically enjoy the stunning "Avenue of Royal Palms," diverse tree species, and guided tours highlighting medicinal plants and history. While cherished for its natural beauty, many visitors note the facility is largely neglected, with dilapidated infrastructure and limited on-site dining
Nature at its best. One of the hidden gems in Africa. Went there for my anniversary celebration. The greenery is amazing and the history behind the trees unbelievable

Natur super, Tiere absolut unerträglich. Da wir an Ostermontag hier waren, war der Park sehr gut besucht, überall waren Familien, die Picknicks hatten, die Kinder haben gespielt, überall wurde Musik gemacht. Trotzdem konnte man die Schönheit des Parks sehen. Was aber gar nicht geht, ist der sogenannte Minizoo. Hier werden Tiere auf die erbärmlichste Art gehalten. Für uns war es unerträglich, dies anzuschauen. Dieser Zoo ist in einem Botanischen Garten absolut nicht notwendig

Lovely botanical garden. Visited the botanical gardens. Yaw was our guide and he did a very good job. The gardens are extensive so we didn't get round the whole area. The information given was extremely interesting. We were short on time and wanted to visit the waterfall so we cut this short. Well worth a visit and if you get a guide then it can be really useful
Tree variety. Beautiful trees but lots of rubbish everywhere which rather spoiled the effect. Main path with tall palms is grand and calm

It is cool and calm to visit here. for recreational purpose and vacation... I'll recommend 10/10 everyone. I love nature and the fact that this garden has so much to share and enlightenment… thank you to our great guide Martin! Very patient and full of knowledge. Next time I’ll be prepared to embark on the jungle trail… says the soldier in me! ☺️ but in this garden you’ll find cooking spices and medicinal trees and even a “snake tree” 😳… peaceful grounds, a lovely place to pray and meditate and lots of trees rather giant size or unique stature. I’ll definitely visit again. The little shops are also nice to visit …

Peaceful Aburi Botanical Gardens. Oasis of calm so close to busy Accra. We had one of the official garden guides who spent an hour explaining the main attractions there. He was great, very engaging and explained what certain plants were used for and how to recognise them as well as the history of the garden. The gardens themselves are an interesting mix of plants from around the world, nicely kept paths and you can easily spend an hour walking on flat paths, although there are some stepped routes if you want to ramble more
Average. Very difficult stone paths are uneven I agree, it's pretty, but not well maintained. it felt like a zoo without animals to me. Just average

Beautiful, tranquil setting with excellent guides. Quiet, lovely location. The weather is cooler, the atmosphere is serene. Our guide Quartey was excellent, and we learnt about the history of the Botanical Gardens as well as a number of fantastic trees, plants and shrubs. Seeing and tasting cocoa fruit was a great experience, and there were food and souvenir stalls with a delicious fruit salad, freshly made and beautifully served

What a let down. Poorly maintained tourist attraction. Moss covered poorly maintained paths, overgrown lawns, weeds everywhere, rusty signage, dilapidated buildings. We were charged 20 Cedis which is twice tourist price and 4 times local residents entrance fee. What are they using the money for? Where is the management or tourist board, who is accountable for false advertising to tourists? The staff blame the government for lack of investment but they sit around chatting and have no pride in their country, just try to guide you to the souvenirs. Left very disappointed as had been looking forward to a relaxing walk through a beautiful botanical garden but it’s a dump

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Don’t miss the falls!. Thoroughly enjoyed this trip. The falls were the highlight as we went during the rainy season when they were in full force - incredible place. Really enjoyed the botanical gardens as well. Make sure to take some small notes to tip the villagers at the Umbrella rock. Great communication from our guide and driver, and despite someone driving into the back of our car, they kept calm and we always felt safe. Highly recommend!

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Search for another tour. I am giving this tour three stars based primarily on my interaction with the tour owner. The night before the tour, I confirmed my 7:00 a.m. hotel pickup with the operator via WhatsApp. The next morning, at 7:05 a.m., I called three times with no answer. I then contacted Viator, who also received no response and stated they would follow up by email. At 7:44 a.m., the operator finally contacted me to apologize, explaining that he had misplaced his phone and that the driver was waiting at the wrong hotel. After exchanging messages and providing proof of my reservation showing the correct hotel, I was told the driver would arrive within five minutes—which, due to Accra traffic, turned into about 30 minutes. While I did not expect a full refund, I did feel some compensation for the delay and confusion was warranted. I was offered $17 USD, which I ultimately declined out of frustration. The tour guide, Isaac, communicated that he was stuck in traffic and arrived around 8:30 a.m. He was very apologetic, friendly, and made the rest of the day enjoyable. He was engaging, assisted with photos and translations, drove safely, and provided bottled water. Although I would not recommend this tour due to the owner’s lack of communication, the Botanical Gardens and Boti Waterfalls are definitely worth visiting—just perhaps with a different company at a better price. Tip: Even if you don’t plan to swim, bring a swimsuit for photos in the water. There is a changing area available

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Such a nice tour.. This is such a nice tour. The botanical garden and the cocoa farm are really nice - lush and educational. The waterfalls are exceptionally beautiful, very picturesque. The guide Kwaku is one of the best guides we ever had - and the driver Kofi did a fantastic job in the Ghanaian traffic. We felt safe at all times. Highly recommended

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Highly Recommended Experience. My family and I had the best time on this tour with Kweku as the guide. Kweku was very professional and super knowledgeable. We were about to learn a lot. Kweku was extremely organized. We knew what we were about to do every step of the way. The tour is an all day tour so we packed our lunch. We were able to sit down and eat before doing the tour of Boti Falls. I recommend bringing food for conveniency. I highly recommend!

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Great day tour, highly recommended. We had a wonderful day seeing some of the sights around Ghana on this tour. Our guides were very friendly, knowledgeable and always keen to please. After our hotel pickup we drove to Aburi Botanical Gardens which was very picturesque. Then we spent some time at Tetteh Quarshie cocoa farm, followed by Asenema Waterfalls. Overall the day was plenty of fun, mostly because of our guides. Highly recommend this tour

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Nice tour in Ghana's country side. The nature garden was interesting. Learned alot about the fauna. We were allowed to handle some of the leaves, bark, fruit and seeds. That was very informative as well. Really enjoyed the coco farm tour. Learning the difference between Ghana cocoa and South America's. Being able to taste the different cocoa was a plus. Purchased black soap n chocolates. Too bad Boti Falls were dry but we did Asenema which were quite refreshing. We finished with a nice traditional Ghanian lunch that was delicious. Kofi our tour guide was very informative and polite. He pointed out many sites along the way. He was very accommodating in the morning at pick-up. He answered all of our questions

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Enjoy nature. Very good. Loved the Boti Falls, gardens, and coco farm. Would like to hear more about the regions as part of the tour and maybe more knowledge on the falls (insects, vegetation). Maybe do two of the sites, lunch and then the last sight instead of all three back to back

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Love the Farm and the Falls.. First Michael and Samson were awesome guides. My top favorites were the Cocoa Farm and the Boti Falls. The falls were made even more special because we hike two summits prior to visiting it. So the falls and the crystal water was the prize. The Tetteh quarshie Cocoa was simply amazing. Michael my guide at the farm was patient knowledgeable and provided an enlightened presentation

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Would book with them again!. Isaac and Emmanuel were excellent guides on this tour. Isaac was knowledgeable and accommodating and Emmanuel was able to get us to and from safe and sound especially when going through areas with difficult roads. They were professional and I felt safe traveling as a solo woman. The tours were amazing and I would recommend anyone interested to book with them. Thank you guys for an amazing time!

place_name: Experience Botiwaterfall, Aburi Botanical Gardens & a Cocoa Farm.
text: Simply Amazing. Our tour was amazing! First to the botanical garden where we took so many pictures and the guide was so knowledgeable then we were off to the cocoa farm. Both were amazing but NOTHING can compare to the Boti Falls! I was afraid of the steps but I was able to concur them down and back up! The falls were peaceful and beautiful and simply amazing! My husband and I took so many pictures for memories of Ghana! So happy we booked this tour and Michael was awesome! He stopped and got us local snacks, water and fruit on the way home! Overall we would give this a 10 rating!!!!!
